questions.def: "Once" introduces a time clause indicating a single point in time.
questions.question: ___ I finish this report, I'll go home.

questions.def: "As soon as" shows immediacy after an event in a time clause.
questions.question: I'll call you ___ I arrive at the hotel.

questions.def: Use present perfect continuous for actions starting in the past.
questions.question: We ___ for the bus since noon.

questions.def: "When" introduces a time clause, denoting a specific moment.
questions.question: ___ the rain stops, we can go for a walk.

questions.def: "After" indicates a sequence of events in the past.
questions.question: ___ I had finished my work, I went out.

questions.def: Past perfect indicates an action before another past action.
questions.question: They ___ here before moving to London.

questions.def: "If" expresses a condition related to a time.
questions.question: I'll be there ___ you need me.

questions.def: "After" correctly indicates sequence of events.
questions.question: He started working ___ he graduated.

questions.def: Past perfect continuous for duration before a past event.
questions.question: By the time he arrived, she ___ for hours.

questions.def: "Whenever" indicates every time the event occurs.
questions.question: ___ I see him, I will tell him the news.

questions.def: "Until" indicates the end point of a period.
questions.question: I'll wait ___ you're ready.

questions.def: Present perfect follows 'as soon as' for future actions.
questions.question: As soon as I ___ the email, I'll send it.

questions.def: "While" shows simultaneous actions or states.
questions.question: ___ you are working, please do not disturb me.

questions.def: "By the time" sets a deadline before another event.
questions.question: She had already left ___ I arrived.

questions.def: Present perfect for actions starting in the past and continuing.
questions.question: I ___ him since we were children.

questions.def: "As" can introduce a time clause indicating a simultaneous action.
questions.question: ___ I was walking home, I saw an accident.

questions.def: "Since" indicates a starting point in the past.
questions.question: He hadn't eaten ___ yesterday.

questions.def: Past simple for the earlier event in a 'before' clause.
questions.question: Before I ___, they had already started.

questions.def: "By" indicates a deadline or completion point.
questions.question: ___ the end of the week, I'll finish the project.

questions.def: "Once" indicates the moment of completion.
questions.question: ___ he finishes, we can leave.

questions.def: Use "While" when referring to the duration of an action.
questions.question: During I was on holiday, I relaxed.

questions.def: Future simple in the main clause with 'until'.
questions.question: I ___ here until you come back.

questions.def: "If" introduces a conditional time-related clause.
questions.question: Call me ___ you have any questions.

questions.def: "For" indicates a duration of time.
questions.question: He's been working here ___ five years.

questions.def: Use present perfect in the time clause when the main clause is future.
questions.question: Once I ___ my degree, I'll travel the world.

questions.def: Past perfect not needed because 'by the time' indicates the time frame.
questions.question: By the time the meeting ___, everyone was exhausted.

questions.def: 'While' + present continuous is fine, but simpler is better here.
questions.question: While I am waiting, I will read a book.

questions.def: 'When' is the most appropriate conjunction in this time clause.
questions.question: We will start ___ they get here.

questions.def: 'As soon as' indicates immediate action following another.
questions.question: I'll call you ___ I get home from work.

questions.def: 'After' correctly indicates the sequence of events.
questions.question: ___ he had finished eating, he left the restaurant.
